name: Anhanguera
sum: Iconic crested ornithocheiriform from the Early Cretaceous of Brazil (Romualdo Formation), with rounded crests on the jaws and a spoon-shaped tooth rosette.
wsnote: Wingspan of about 4.6 m for the largest specimens.
holotype: Type species A. blittersdorffi, based on a complete skull from Romualdo Formation concretions, Ceará–Pernambuco, Brazil.
material: Complete skulls; A. piscator is known from a nearly complete three-dimensional skeleton.
biology: Fish-eater: long, angled conical teeth in a rosette for seizing slippery prey near the water surface. Jaw crests varied between individuals and may relate to age or sex.
author: Campos and Kellner 1985
